chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a basket of unripened dates as a debt upon him, so he takes from him a basket of fresh dates, and these are fewer than those. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' I said: 'Suppose there is for me a basket of unripened dates as a debt upon him, so I take from him a basket of ripe dates, and these are more than those?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem, if it is well-known between you two.'
ai.seo_question: Can I repay a debt of unripened dates with ripe dates?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of settling a debt in a different form of the same commodity (e.g., unripened dates for fresh dates) with varying quantities, provided the exchange is a recognized custom ('ma'rufan') between the parties. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that mutual consent and established local practice can validate such exchanges, distinguishing them from strict usury (riba) by focusing on the agreed-upon nature of the transaction rather than rigid equivalence. This ruling underscores the flexibility in commercial jurisprudence when dealing with perishable goods where quality and ripeness fluctuate.
